docs.title: Welcome to the DIFFER-PLD4E-schemas documentation
docs.text: A NOMAD plugin with the electronic lab notebook (ELN) schemas of the PLD4Energy lab at DIFFER.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
The plugin adds these entry types to NOMAD:

Entry type Use it for SA-PLD Logbook One run on the SA-PLD system: the samples it makes or processes, system details, laser calibration, targets, process steps and in-situ data. LA-PLD Logbook One run on the LA-PLD system. Same as SA-PLD, plus the larger carriers, the particle reduction plate and polar/cartesian heater scans. SPS Logbook One run on the SPS sputter system: the samples, substrate carrier and mask, targets (positions 1 to 3) and process steps (pre-sputtering, heating, sputtering, cool-down). PLD Target One physical PLD target (the PLD target database). Sputter Target One physical sputter target, with its diameter (the sputter target database). Substrate type One kind of substrate, e.g. SrTiO3 10x10 mm (the substrate database, shared by all systems). Sample One sample: a substrate with the films grown on it, with its sample ID. Usually created for you by a logbook; not specific to one system. PLD In-situ Techniques In-situ measurements (RHEED, MIC, SE, LA-EDS, OES, SHG) that are not part of a new deposition run, e.g. post-processing of an older sample.

It also adds two logbook dashboards, the PLD logbook (SA-PLD and LA-PLD) and the Sputter logbook (SPS): guided forms that start from the samples, show only the fields that apply, and only save complete logbooks (unfinished runs can be kept as drafts). See Use the logbook dashboards.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: This page explains how the PLD schemas are put together and why. It is background for users who want to understand the behaviour, and for maintainers who change the schemas.

docs.title: From the mock-up to NOMAD
docs.text:
The schemas started from the PLD4Energy ELN mock-up (an HTML form) and the users' feedback on it. The mock-up is a form, not a data model, so repeated parts of the form became reusable sections:

In the mock-up In the schema The gas checkboxes and flow fields, repeated in every step One BackgroundGas section, repeated per gas in every step; the shared valve and the UHV / Background gas choice on the step Laser fields, repeated in pre-ablation and deposition One LaserParameters section (laser) "Substrate stage start x/y/z/tilt/spin-position" One HeaterStagePosition section with x, y, z, tilt, spin Target stage fields One TargetStage section Laser details in the system details LaserCalibration (laser_details) Fields shown only for a choice (scan yes/no, polar/cartesian) Optional sub-sections, added on save for the chosen option "Number of targets/samples" counters Repeating sub-sections: add as many as you need In-situ techniques inside the deposition step Separate in_situ_measurements and a stand-alone entry type

NOMAD forms cannot show or hide a field depending on another field. Conditional fields are therefore optional sub-sections. The section for the chosen option is added on save, so its fields appear without having to add it by hand.

docs.title: Entries and how they refer to each other
docs.text:
SA-PLD / LA-PLD Logbook (entry)
├── samples[]
│   ├── substrate ──────────► Substrate type (entry)
│   ├── layers[] ── target ─► PLD Target (entry)
│   └── reference ──────────► Sample (entry; new and external samples: created on save)
│                               ├── substrate ──► Substrate type
│                               └── layers[] ── target ──► PLD Target
├── laser_details
├── targets[] ── target ────► PLD Target
├── load_recipe ── recipe ──► earlier logbook of the same system
├── steps[]
│   ├── Pre-ablation step ── target ──► PLD Target
│   ├── Heating step
│   ├── Annealing step
│   ├── Pulsed laser deposition step ── target, samples[] ──► PLD Target, Sample
│   └── Cool-down step
└── in_situ_measurements[] ── sample, process_steps[] ──► Sample, steps of this logbook

PLD In-situ Techniques (entry) ── sample ──► Sample

Targets, substrate types, samples and logbooks are separate entries because each one has its own life:

  • A target is used in many runs. Storing it once means its material, manufacturer and purchase date are entered once, and every run that used it can be found from the target.
  • A sample outlives the run that made it: it is measured later, post-processed, gets another film in a later run, or is used with a recipe. In-situ measurements and later runs refer to it.
  • A logbook is one run.

NOMAD's reference picker searches for other entries; it cannot pick a section inside the entry being edited. This is a second reason why targets and samples are their own entries: steps can then pick them from a drop-down.

docs.title: Samples and substrates
docs.text:
A substrate is the template a film is grown on; after the deposition the sample is the substrate with its films. Researchers start a run from the samples they will make or process, so a logbook starts with a list of samples (SampleInRun). Each is one of:

  • a new sample: a substrate from the substrate database;
  • an external sample: prepared elsewhere, without a sample ID, so its substrate can also be described freely, together with the films it already has (prior_layers);
  • an existing sample: made earlier in a PLD4Energy system and referenced, for an extra deposition, an annealing or only characterisation.

New and external samples get a sample ID <system>_<yyyy-mm-dd>_<hh:mm>_S<nn> from the start of the run on the lab clock, numbered in the order of the list after the highest number already given (a removed sample's number is not given again, so it cannot take over that sample's entry), and a name made from the substrate and films (SrTiO3_YSZ-20nm_SrRuO3-50nm). The ID identifies the sample and never changes once its entry exists; the name describes it. On save the logbook creates a Sample entry for each of them (using create_archive from nomad-material-processing) and links it. The file is named after the sample ID and records the logbook file that made it (made_in). If a file with that name already exists, it is linked rather than overwritten, so Sample entries are never replaced by accident; but only if this logbook made it: a file made by another logbook is not linked, and an error is logged. Files from before made_in existed are linked with a warning. A sample ID that an earlier version made from the start in UTC is kept when its file exists. An existing sample's entry is never changed by a logbook: it may be in another or in a published upload. The films grown on it in this run are recorded in the logbook.

Substrates and film materials come from databases, like the targets: a Substrate type entry per kind of substrate (material and size), and each film refers to the target it is grown from, which gives its material.

The films are not entered with the samples: each deposition step grows one film on its samples, from the step's target and with its film thickness. The dashboard derives the films of every sample from the steps, in order. The targets of a run are therefore selected once, under Targets, and the sample name always follows what was deposited. New substrates and targets can so be added by the users, without a change to the plugin, and the sample names always use the materials as entered there.

The Sample section (sample.py) knows nothing about PLD: it records the system it was made in as text. The same section and the SampleRun base of the logbook are therefore also used by the SPS logbook, and can be used by later diagnostics, so a sample made in one system can be processed and measured in another.

docs.title: SA-PLD and LA-PLD
docs.text:
Both logbooks share the PLDLogbook base: samples, system details, laser details, targets, recipe, in-situ techniques and all step logic. They differ only in:

SA-PLD LA-PLD Substrate carriers Omicron, 1" Omicron, 1", 4" wafer, sample select Particle reduction plate – in use / not in use Samples of a deposition step the samples ticked in its sample mask (all by default) the chosen sample Deposition step scan substrate stage scan yes/no + scan width and speed heater scan type: polar (default) or cartesian

Each system has its own step classes (SAPLDStep and LAPLDStep and their subclasses). When you add a step, NOMAD offers all sections that inherit from the step type of the steps sub-section. Separate step classes mean an SA-PLD logbook offers only SA-PLD steps. The SPS logbook works the same way with SPSStep, so a sputter step is never offered in a PLD logbook and a PLD step never in the SPS logbook. The shared content of the steps (pre-ablation, heating, annealing, deposition, cool-down) lives in common base classes, so it is defined only once; the parts every system has (pressure, background gases, heating and cool-down) are in process_steps.py and shared with the SPS.

docs.title: The SPS logbook
docs.text:
The SPSLogbook (sps_deposition.py) follows the PLD logbooks: it is a SampleRun, so its samples, sample IDs (SPS_...) and names work the same, and its targets come from a database, the Sputter Target entries. These are separate from the PLD targets: a sputter target is a different object, with a diameter that decides which of the three positions it fits (1 and 2: 2", 3: 4"). Each pre-sputtering or sputtering step records the plasma (DC, RF or both) in its own SputterPlasma sub-section. Every sputtering step grows a film on the samples ticked in its sample mask (all by default), like an SA-PLD deposition.

The power ramps are noted in the lab per 5 minutes. pint, which converts the units, cannot express "per 5 minutes", so they are stored as rates (W/s, shown in W/min) and the dashboard converts from W/5 min with a scale on the form field.

docs.title: Generated (read-only) fields
docs.text:
Some fields have no input box: they are filled in by the plugin on save. This is on purpose: these values are derived from other fields or from another entry, and typing them by hand would let them disagree with their source.

Field Where Why it is read-only How to change it PVD system logbook Fixed by the logbook type. A free choice would allow an "SA-PLD" logbook with LA-PLD carriers and steps. Use the other logbook type. Sample ID samples in the logbook, Sample Built as <system>_<yyyy-mm-dd>_<hh:mm>_S<nn>, so IDs always follow the same pattern. Kept once filled in, because labels and later runs refer to it. Before the first save: change the system, start or order of the samples. Sample UUID samples in the logbook, Sample Derived from the sample ID (UUID version 5), so it is the same however often the entry is processed, and kept once stored, because it is printed on QR labels. The Sample entry owns it: a run copies it from there. Editing it would break the link between a label and its sample. Not changeable. Substrate material and size Sample Taken from the substrate. Change the substrate. Material, manufacturer, purchase date targets in the logbook Copied from the PLD Target entry, for checking your selection. Correct the PLD Target entry. Target number pre-ablation and deposition steps Copied from the target details, so the steps always show the number the target has in this run. Change it in the target details. Data status in-situ techniques Whether a data file has been added. Add a data file. Elemental composition targets, substrate types Follows from the chemical formula. Correct the chemical formula. Elements of a film or sample samples, films Those of the targets and the substrate type. Correct the formula on the target or substrate type. sources, environment, sample_parameters process steps The native NOMAD view of what was entered (see Search). Change the step's own fields. Applied recipe load recipe A record of what was applied. Apply a recipe. Energy, intensity LA-EDS Calculated from / read from the spectrum. Change E0 or the energy per channel.

The sample name is generated too, but can be overwritten: it only describes the sample.

Note

The 1st window transmission is calculated but not read-only: you can override it, see below.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
NOMAD's search (Explore) only knows what is stored in its own, native sections. A material typed as text, e.g. material: SrTiO3, is a string to NOMAD: it cannot be searched by element or formula. Every entry type of the plugin therefore extends a native NOMAD section, and the plugin fills the native parts from what is entered:

Entry Native section Searchable as PLD / Sputter Target CompositeSystem (PLD: nomad-material-processing PLDTarget) elements and formula, from chemical_formula; the engraved ID as lab ID Substrate type nomad-material-processing CrystallineSubstrate elements and formula, from chemical_formula Sample CompositeSystem elements of the substrate and of the films (from their targets); the sample ID as lab ID SA-PLD / LA-PLD logbook nomad-material-processing PulsedLaserDeposition method Pulsed Laser Deposition; elements of the films grown SPS logbook nomad-material-processing SputterDeposition method Sputter Deposition; elements of the films grown In-situ measurement Measurement methods In-situ diagnostics and the techniques used (e.g. RHEED)

Chemical formula. Lab names are not formulas: NOMAD reads 8YSZ as yttrium, sulfur and an unknown element, and STO as sulfur and oxygen. Targets and substrate types therefore have a chemical_formula next to the material name, e.g. (Y2O3)0.08(ZrO2)0.92 for 8YSZ; the name stays what the lab calls it and is used in sample names. A formula with unknown element symbols is rejected with an error on save, and the entry then has no elements. A wrong formula made of real element symbols cannot be detected, so check the formula when adding a target.

Films and samples. A film (Layer, a native ThinFilm) takes the elements of its target, without fractions: a sample combines several films and a substrate, whose fractions would not add up. A film is part of its Sample entry rather than an entry of its own, so the sample's elements never depend on other entries being processed first. A logbook contains the films grown in the run under its samples, so it is found by those elements too.

Steps. The process steps are native vapour deposition steps. Besides their own fields, the plugin fills in their native environment (pressure, gas flows), sources (the target and the laser or plasma power) and sample_parameters (substrate temperature). These are read-only copies: change the step's own fields.

docs.title: Laser calibration
docs.text:
The laser energy is measured before and after the chamber, so the beam passes both windows between the two readings:

E_after = E_before × T1 × T2   →   T1 = E_after / (E_before × T2)

T2 (the 2nd window) is 92 % by default. T1 is calculated on every save unless transmission window 1 manual is ticked and a value is entered; then the typed value is kept. With a missing energy, or an energy before the chamber of 0, nothing is calculated.

The calibration and the targets are only needed when a step of the run uses the laser. See Laser and targets follow the process steps.

Formula to be confirmed

The mock-up wrote the formula as E_after / E_before × T₂. Read literally ((E_after / E_before) × T2) that contradicts E_after = E_before × T1 × T2, so the schema uses E_after / (E_before × T2). If the literal formula is meant, change transmission_window_1() in laser.py.

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text:
A recipe is not a separate entry type: any earlier logbook of the same system can be used as one. Applying it copies the process steps into the current logbook. Copying a snapshot, rather than linking to the recipe, means:

  • the new logbook records exactly what was done in this run, even if the recipe logbook is edited later;
  • the copied steps can be changed for this run without changing the recipe.

The recipe field keeps the link to where the steps came from.

The copy keeps references to targets, but replaces the samples of deposition steps with the samples of this run (or the one chosen in the recipe loader). This is how "do not copy the sample identity" is implemented. References to entries in the recipe's upload are rewritten to absolute references, so they still point to the right entry when the recipe comes from another upload.

The copy is triggered by a tick box (apply_recipe) that is unticked after the copy. Saving again therefore does not copy again. See Reproduce a run with a recipe for the details.

docs.title: Units
docs.text:
Values are stored in SI units (Pa, J, m, K, s, ...) and shown in the units of the lab (mbar, mJ, mm, nm, °C, min, ...). You type values in the shown unit in the form. In archive files (YAML/JSON) values must be given in the SI unit.

Exceptions, stored as plain numbers:

  • percentages (window transmissions, attenuator position, heater output, control box output), in %;
  • the valve position, from 0 (closed) to 1000 (open);
  • gas flows are stored in cm³/min, which is the same number as sccm.

Ramp rates are in K/min, which is the same number as °C/min. Temperatures are stored in K and shown in °C.

docs.title: In-situ techniques
docs.text:
In-situ techniques are their own section and not part of a deposition step, because a sample can be measured outside a deposition run, e.g. during post-processing of an older sample. They can be recorded in the logbook of the run or in a stand-alone PLD In-situ Techniques entry. In a logbook each measurement names its sample and the process steps it was taken during; the stand-alone entry has optional links to a sample and to a run.

For each technique the native file (which only the instrument software can open) and the exported file (which other programs can read) are stored separately where both exist. The data are often collected from several computers after the run, so a technique can be saved without files: its data_status is then awaiting data, with a warning on every save, until a file is added. The run's metadata is safe in NOMAD in the meantime, and the missing data stays visible.

The LA-EDS energy axis is not stored in the .sp0 file and is rebuilt from E0 and the energy per channel. The .sp0 reader is still to be written; the LA-EDS spectrum supplier changes from RSX1000 to RaySpec RSX2000, so the reader is kept separate and easy to replace.

docs.title: The logbook dashboards
docs.text: The dashboards live in src/differ_pld4e_schemas/dashboards/ (pld_logbook/, sputter_logbook/ and the shared common/). They are part of this plugin, so the forms and the schemas they write are always released together. This section explains why they exist and how they behave; Plugin structure maps their code, endpoints and checks for developers.

docs.title: Why a dashboard
docs.text:
The NOMAD entry editor shows every field of a schema section and lets you save at any time. It cannot hide a field depending on another field, and it cannot refuse to save an incomplete entry. For the PLD logbooks this means users see LA-PLD fields on SA-PLD runs, polar and cartesian scan fields at the same time, and logbooks can be saved half-empty.

A dashboard plugin is a FastAPI app that NOMAD mounts under <NOMAD URL>/dashboards/<id>/, so it runs on the same origin as NOMAD and can use the NOMAD API with the user's session. The PLD logbook dashboard uses that to offer its own form with conditional fields and a completeness check, and then writes normal NOMAD entries of the PLD4Energy schemas.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
browser (static/*.js)                       dashboard app (FastAPI)
  form, live checks  ── GET  api/spec ──►     spec.py   form definition
                     ── POST api/archive ─►   rules.py  validation (again)
                     ◄─ archive files ────    convert.py form ⇄ archive (SI units)
                     ── POST api/draft-name   (where a draft is kept)
                     ── POST api/form-from-archive (open logbook / recipe)

browser ──► NOMAD API (with the user's session)
  /users/me, /uploads, /entries/query, /entries/archive/query,
  PUT/GET/DELETE /uploads/<id>/raw/...  (in-situ files, drafts, archives)
  GET /uploads/<id>/rawdir/<draft_dir>  (list drafts)
  • spec.py is the single definition of the form: sections, fields, units, choices, which fields are required and when a field is shown (visible_if). The browser renders the form from it and the server validates against it.
  • rules.py computes values (1st window transmission, sample IDs and names), how much of a section the process steps need, and validates a form. static/rules.js contains the same rules so problems show while typing; the server always validates again before it builds anything.
  • convert.py turns a complete form into archive files and reads saved logbooks back into a form.

The sputter logbook dashboard (dashboards/sputter_logbook/) has its own spec.py, rules.py and convert.py, and shares everything else with the PLD logbook in dashboards/common/: the same page (static/) and FastAPI app (app.py), the rules (LogbookRules in rules.py), the conversion of the parts every logbook has (LogbookConverter in convert.py) and the field groups every system has (steps.py). The page itself knows no system: what differs (title, texts, draft folder, which steps grow films) comes from the client part of the form definition. Also shared:

  • fields.py builds field definitions;
  • values.py evaluates conditions and reads form values;
  • archive.py maps form values to archive quantities, converting from the unit of the form field to the unit of the schema quantity with pint;
  • samples.py is the Samples section: its fields, sample IDs and names, and the Sample files.

docs.title: Laser and targets follow the process steps
docs.text:
Each step type declares whether it needs the laser: required (pre-ablation, deposition), optional or none (heating, annealing, cool-down). A section with requirement: {'from_steps': 'laser'}, the laser details and the targets, is needed as much as the step that needs it most:

Steps of the run Laser details and targets at least one step needs the laser required a step may use the laser optional: saved if filled in no step uses the laser not needed: not checked and not saved

A step type with an optional laser gets a Laser used switch in front of its laser fields; once switched on, that step counts as needing the laser. No PLD step uses this yet; it is there for step types to come.

docs.title: Completeness
docs.text:
A field is required when it is visible and marked required. Hidden fields are never required, so choosing Cartesian scan makes the cartesian fields required and the polar fields irrelevant. Lists have a minimum number of items and unique values (targets, target numbers, sample IDs, existing samples). In-situ data files are not required: a technique without files is saved as awaiting data.

The save button stays disabled while anything is missing, and api/archive refuses to build archive files for an incomplete form, so incomplete logbooks cannot be written through the dashboard.

docs.title: Drafts
docs.text:
Users must log every step of a run, also external users of the facility, but a run is often filled in on several computers. Saving incomplete logbooks would let half-logged runs end up in NOMAD as data. Instead, an unfinished run can be saved as a draft: the form state as a plain JSON file, <draft dir>/<system>_<date>_<hhmm>[_<run name>].draft.json, in the upload (pld_drafts for the PLD logbook, sps_drafts for the sputter logbook).

  • No NOMAD parser reads .draft.json files, so a draft is never an entry: it is not searchable, creates no Sample entries and does not count as logged.
  • Any computer can continue it (the start page lists the drafts in the user's unpublished uploads). In-situ files picked for a draft are uploaded with it.
  • Before a draft is overwritten, it is read again: if another computer saved it in the meantime, the user chooses which version to keep.
  • The final save creates the entries and deletes the draft.

A draft only needs the system, date and start time, which name the file. The form is also kept in the browser's local storage, as a safeguard on the same computer.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text:
1. The page checks that the NOMAD session is still valid. The form, without the files not uploaded yet, is validated by the server, which also returns the file name of the logbook (<system>_<date>_<hhmm>[_<run name>].archive.json). A new logbook whose file already exists stops the save here, before anything is uploaded.
  2. In-situ and log files are uploaded, one request per file (NOMAD only waits for processing of a request with a single file), to <file dir>/<system>_<date>_<hhmm>[_<run name>]/<section>/<field>/, e.g. .../in_situ/rheed_roi_intensity_export_files/ (<file dir> is pld_files for the PLD logbook, sps_files for the sputter logbook). Each technique has its own folder, and a file never replaces another: a name already in the folder (or added twice) gets a number, step1 (2).txt. The server validates the form again, now with the uploaded file paths.
  3. One Sample archive is written per new or external sample, named after its sample ID, and the logbook archive refers to it by file name. A Sample that this logbook created before is written again (overwritten), so corrections made in the dashboard reach it, but only through the file its sample ID gives; existing samples of other runs are never written.
  4. The logbook is written. A new logbook never overwrites an existing file; an opened logbook is overwritten if it was made by the dashboard (its file is named <system>_<date>_<hhmm>[_<run name>].archive.json). Other logbooks, e.g. hand-written .archive.yaml files, are saved as a new logbook in the same upload instead.
  5. The draft of the run, if any, is deleted.

Data files, Sample and logbook archives are written with wait_for_processing=true, so the next write does not find the upload busy and NOMAD's processing errors and warnings are shown in the log. Drafts are written without waiting: NOMAD does not make entries of them.

A file chosen in the form is kept in the form's list as pending:<id>/<name> until it is uploaded (static/files.js), so it stays with its measurement when measurements are moved or removed. The server refuses a form that still holds one. A save that ends after another logbook was put in the form leaves that logbook as it is.

Run and step times are on the lab's clock: its time zone (lab_time_zone, default Europe/Amsterdam) turns a date and hh:mm into an instant, with the offset of that date (+01:00 in winter, +02:00 in summer). NOMAD stores the instants in UTC; opening a logbook turns them back into the lab's clock, so a logbook reads and saves the same wherever it is opened. Durations are real elapsed times, also over a clock change. A run time the clock skipped (02:00 to 03:00 on the last Sunday of March) is refused. The sample IDs use the lab's clock and are kept once their entries exist.

docs.title: Conditional fields
docs.text:
Conditions are small JSON objects, evaluated in the browser and on the server:

{'key': 'heater_scan_type', 'equals': 'Polar scan'}  # same step
{'key': '/run/system', 'equals': 'LA-PLD'}  # anywhere in the form
{'key': 'origin', 'in': ['New sample', 'External sample']}
{'key': '/steps', 'has_type': ['deposition']}  # a step of a type exists
{'all': [...]} / {'any': [...]}  # combinations

Choices can also depend on another field (options_by), e.g. the substrate carriers depend on the PVD system.

docs.title: Plugin structure
docs.text: This page is the map of the plugin for developers: what the parts are, where they live, how they talk to each other, what is checked where, and where to make a change. Read it before your first change; the contributing guide has the recipes for the common changes, and the explanation gives the reasons behind the data model.

docs.title: The plugin in one picture
docs.text:
The plugin adds two things to NOMAD: schemas (the entry types of the lab's electronic notebook) and logbook dashboards (guided forms that write entries of those schemas).

                        ┌──────────────────────── NOMAD ────────────────────────┐
 pyproject.toml         │                                                        │
 [nomad.plugin]  ──────►│  schema package  ──►  processes archive files into     │
 entry points           │  (src/.../*.py)       entries: normalize(), search     │
                        │                                                        │
                        │  dashboards      ──►  FastAPI apps mounted at          │
                        │  (src/.../dashboards)  /dashboards/<id>/               │
                        └───────────▲───────────────────────────▲───────────────┘
                                    │ api/spec, api/archive, …   │ NOMAD API with the
                                    │ (form logic)               │ user's session:
                        ┌───────────┴────────────────────────────┴───────────────┐
                        │ browser: static/*.js — the form; writes archive files,  │
                        │ drafts and data files into the user's upload            │
                        └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

The dashboards never write to NOMAD themselves: the dashboard app only turns a form into archive files (JSON), and the page writes them into an upload through the NOMAD API, with the user's own permissions. NOMAD then processes them with the plugin's schemas, exactly like files uploaded by hand. A logbook made with the dashboard and one made in NOMAD's entry editor are the same kind of entry.

docs.title: Repository map
docs.text:
differ-pld4energy-schemas/
├── src/differ_pld4e_schemas/
│   ├── __init__.py              the shared metainfo package (m_package)

docs.title: Part 1: the schemas
docs.text:
Each entry type is a section class that extends a native NOMAD section (e.g. PulsedLaserDeposition, CompositeSystem), so NOMAD's search finds entries by method, elements and lab ID; see Search.

  • One package. All modules define their sections in one metainfo package (differ_pld4e_schemas/__init__.py); schema_packages/schema_package.py imports every module and gives the package its final name. Entry types are stored as differ_pld4e_schemas.schema_packages.schema_package.<Section>, so renaming a section breaks existing entries (why).
  • Save logic lives in normalize() of the sections: sample IDs and names, creating Sample entries, copying target details, applying recipes, filling the native search sections. NOMAD normalizes sub-sections before their parents.
  • Systems are kept apart by class hierarchy: a step must inherit from its system's step class (SAPLDStep, LAPLDStep, SPSStep) to be offered in that logbook; shared content lives in base classes and process_steps.py.
  • Exported data files (RHEED, MIC) are read in in_situ.py. Instrument exports come in several encodings (the MIC export has a Latin-1 header), so they are read as bytes and decoded as a whole (decode_export).

docs.title: The server: one FastAPI app per dashboard
docs.text:
dashboards/<name>/app.py calls common.app.create_app(form_spec, rules, converter) with the dashboard's own three parts:

Part File What it is Form definition (spec) <name>/spec.py Every section and field of the form: kind, unit, schema path (archive), choices, when it is shown (visible_if) and required. Its client part holds the page's texts and settings. Rules <name>/rules.py A LogbookRules: which steps grow films, on which samples, extra computed values. Converter <name>/convert.py A LogbookConverter, plus the sections only this dashboard has (PLD: laser, in-situ).

The app serves:

Endpoint Does GET / The page, with every linked static file versioned by its content (?v=). GET /static/<file> The page's files, always revalidated by the browser (Cache-Control: no-cache, 304 while unchanged). GET /api/spec The form definition, plus script_version (a hash of all static files): when the page and the running server disagree, the page asks for a restart of NOMAD. POST /api/validate Errors and warnings of a form (the page checks locally; used by tests). POST /api/archive Validates again, then returns the archive files to write: one per new or external sample, then the logbook. POST /api/draft-name Where a draft of the form is kept in the upload. POST /api/form-from-archive A saved logbook (or a recipe) read back into a form.

No request is answered with a 500. A body that does not fit the request model (e.g. form is not an object) gets FastAPI's 422; a form whose content has an unexpected shape gets 400 "Malformed form: …" where reading it fails, or a 200 that lists the problems where validation catches them.

docs.title: The form definition is the contract
docs.text:
The spec is plain data (dicts and lists) that both sides read: Python validates and converts with it, the page renders the form from it. Nothing types it, so tests/dashboards/test_spec_contract.py checks every field kind and key (KNOWN_KINDS, FIELD_KEYS in common/fields.py), every condition, the sections and the computed values of both dashboards. When you introduce a key:

  • a field key or kind: add it to KNOWN_KINDS/FIELD_KEYS and the docstring of common/fields.py;
  • a section or step variant key (like requirement, count_control, prefill_from, laser): add it to SECTION_KEYS/VARIANT_KEYS in test_spec_contract.py and to the docstring of pld_logbook/spec.py, which documents them.

docs.title: The page: ES modules without a build step
docs.text:
The browser loads the files in common/static/ as they are: index.html loads app.js as an ES module, which imports the others. There is no bundler and no transpiler; Node is only used to type-check and test them.

Module What Uses app.js The page: start page, form rendering, NOMAD lookups, dialogs, save, drafts, PDF report. Holds the page's state in one app object. rules.js, charts.js, files.js, nomad-api.js, pdf.js, config.js, dom.js, util.js rules.js Computed values and validation, the counterpart of rules.py (createRules(ctx) reads ctx.spec, ctx.refs and ctx.pendingFiles when a rule runs). constants.js, files.js, util.js charts.js Reading and plotting exported data files. dom.js, files.js, util.js files.js Data files chosen but not uploaded yet: the pending:<id>/<name> tokens in the form, and the folders and unique names a save uploads them to. – nomad-api.js Requests to NOMAD (with the session cookie) and to the dashboard's API. config.js, util.js pdf.js A small PDF writer for the report (the sandboxed frame ignores window.print()). – config.js URLs from the page's location: API, GUI, DASHBOARD. – dom.js el(): elements built in code, never from HTML strings. – util.js, constants.js Stateless helpers (dates, file names, upload paths), and values mirrored from Python (NEW_SAMPLE, MADE_HERE, LEVELS; test_page_constants_match_python checks them). –

Rules for the scripts:

  • They never name a system or dashboard: what differs comes from the spec.
  • Modules other than app.js have no state of their own; they get what they need as arguments (see renderFileCharts).
  • A file is type-checked once it starts with // @ts-check (all but app.js so far), using JSDoc types.
  • NOMAD shows the dashboard in a sandboxed frame without allow-modals: window.confirm/alert/prompt/print do nothing, so the page has its own dialogs and makes PDFs itself (a test enforces this).

docs.title: The rules exist twice, and must agree
docs.text:
The page checks the form while you type (rules.js); the server checks it again before it builds anything (rules.py). Python is the reference: it decides what is saved. tests/dashboards/test_js_parity.py runs about 90 forms of both dashboards through the Python rules and keeps the results in tests/js/fixtures/parity.json; tests/js/parity.test.js requires rules.js to give the same errors, warnings, draft errors and computed values. After a deliberate change of the rules:

UPDATE_JS_PARITY=1 uv run pytest tests/dashboards/test_js_parity.py
npm test     # fails until rules.js agrees

In PowerShell, set the variable first: $env:UPDATE_JS_PARITY=1; uv run pytest tests/dashboards/test_js_parity.py; Remove-Item Env:UPDATE_JS_PARITY.

One check is deliberately browser-only: an existing sample whose sample ID is also that of a sample made in the run (the server does not look samples up).

docs.title: What happens when a logbook is saved
docs.text:
page                                   dashboard app                NOMAD API
 │ validate locally (rules.js); check the session ────────────────►  GET users/me
 │ ─ POST api/archive {form without pending files, logbook_file} ──►  validate (rules.py)
 │                                               build files (convert.py)
 │ ◄──────────── files, logbook_file, warnings ─┘
 │ new logbook: stop if its file exists ──────────────────────────►  GET rawdir/<logbook>
 │ per file field: names in its folder, then ─────────────────────►  GET rawdir/<folder>
 │ upload each new file, one request each ────────────────────────►  PUT raw/<file_dir>/<run>/<section>/<field>
 │                                                                     ?overwrite_if_exists=false&wait_for_processing=true
 │ (again api/archive, now with the uploaded file paths)
 │ for each file (samples first, then the logbook) ───────────────►  PUT raw/?file_name=…
 │                                                                     &overwrite_if_exists=…
 │                                                                     &wait_for_processing=true
 │ show NOMAD's processing errors and warnings; delete the draft ──►  DELETE raw/<draft>

<file_dir> and <draft_dir> come from the client part of the spec (pld_files/pld_drafts for PLD, sps_files/sps_drafts for SPS). Drafts are written with wait_for_processing=false: NOMAD does not process them into entries. Drafts are the form state as <draft_dir>/<run>.draft.json; no parser reads them, so they are never entries (see Drafts).

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Setting Where What database_upload_id nomad.yaml at the distribution root (or of the Oasis), under the options of differ_pld4e_schemas.schema_packages:schema_package_entry_point The upload that holds the target and substrate database. Without it the dashboards cannot offer targets or substrates. See Set up the target and substrate database. The tests set a placeholder (tests/conftest.py). lab_time_zone Same place as database_upload_id The IANA time zone of the lab (default Europe/Amsterdam). Run and step times are entered and shown on its clock, and sample IDs use it (time_zone.py). dashboards.enabled NOMAD's nomad.yaml Dashboards are on by default; with false NOMAD serves none. dashboards.frame_ancestors NOMAD's nomad.yaml Origins allowed to show the dashboards in a frame (default: NOMAD itself). Add the origin of another GUI, e.g. the GUI development server, to embed them there.

The options database_upload_id and lab_time_zone are defined on the schema entry point (schema_packages/__init__.py) and read by database.py and time_zone.py, which pass them into the form definition of both dashboards.

docs.title: When the dashboard does not load
docs.text:
• NOMAD mounts each dashboard when it starts. If a dashboard fails to load (an exception in its spec.py, rules.py or convert.py), NOMAD logs an error that names the entry point, skips that dashboard, and its URL answers
  • Look for that error in NOMAD's log.
  • The page compares a version of its files (a hash of static/) with the version the running server took at its start: after a change to static/ it shows "The dashboard was updated, but NOMAD still runs the previous version of it" until NOMAD is restarted (uv run poe start). A change to Python is not detected: restart NOMAD after it as well.

docs.title: What is trusted, and what is checked
docs.text:
The page runs with the user's own NOMAD permissions, so NOMAD decides which uploads a user can write to. Within that, drafts are files in uploads that co-authors can change, and the server cannot see which upload the page writes to, so both sides check:

Risk Checked by A draft that sends the save into another upload The page: checkedEdit keeps a draft's logbook only if it is in the draft's own upload and has a name the dashboard makes; checked again before every save. Overwriting a file that is not the opened logbook The server: is_logbook_file (common/convert.py) allows only {system}_{date}_{hhmm}[_{name}].archive.json; anything else is saved as a new logbook. Overwriting another sample's file The server: own_sample_file (common/samples.py) allows a Sample file only if it is the file of that sample's ID; else the link is kept and a warning shown. Paths that leave the upload or change the request The page: uploadPath (util.js) checks the upload id and encodes every part. Forms of the wrong shape The server: 400 or 422 instead of 500 (malformed_request in common/app.py). Injected HTML The page builds every element with el() and text nodes; there is no innerHTML.

docs.title: Tests and CI
docs.text:
Tests Cover tests/test_pld_schema.py, test_sputter_schema.py The schemas: sections, save logic, recipes, exported data files. tests/test_database.py, test_native_search.py The target and substrate database; the native sections NOMAD searches. tests/test_sample_creation.py The Sample entries the logbook normalizer writes into an upload. tests/schema_packages/ The schema package loads, with an example entry. tests/dashboards/test_pld_logbook.py, test_sputter_logbook.py Each dashboard: spec against the schemas, validation, conversion, the app. tests/dashboards/test_spec_contract.py The form definitions' keys, kinds, conditions and computed values; every number field's unit against the unit of its schema quantity. tests/dashboards/test_processing.py The files each dashboard writes, processed as NOMAD processes an upload (archive parser and all normalizers), with no errors or warnings. tests/dashboards/test_js_parity.py Writes and checks tests/js/fixtures/parity.json. tests/dashboards/test_dashboard_input.py Which files a save may overwrite. tests/dashboards/test_malformed_input.py Malformed requests get a 400, 422 or a 200 listing the problems, never a 500. tests/dashboards/test_page.py The page, versioned and revalidated static files, no blocked dialogs. tests/helpers/ Shared by the tests: the complete forms (pld_forms, sputter_forms), the entries they refer to (database), and nomad_harness, which processes a file like a NOMAD server without mongo or Elasticsearch. tests/ is on the pytest pythonpath. tests/js/*.test.js The scripts: rules, parity, charts, nomad-api, pdf.

Test data: tests/data/example_*.archive.yaml are example entries; tests/data/exports/ holds small RHEED and MIC exports, kept byte for byte (.gitattributes). tests/data/raw_data/ is for large local files and is not in the repository.

Run everything from the plugin folder. In the distribution, uv uses the distribution's environment. For the plugin repository on its own (e.g. in the devcontainer, which has Python and Node but not uv), install uv and run uv sync --all-extras in the plugin folder first, as CI does.

uv run pytest                 # Python: schemas and dashboards
uv run ruff check src tests
npm ci && npm run typecheck && npm test    # the page's scripts (Node 22+)

CI (.github/workflows/actions.yml) runs on every push and pull request: install-and-test (pytest with coverage), dashboard-scripts (type check and JS tests) and ruff-linting (ruff check . on the whole repository, so run uv run ruff check . locally to see the same). Note that CI installs the newest nomad-lab without its infrastructure extras: NOMAD then logs with the standard logging module instead of structlog, which tests that check log messages must allow for. mkdocs-deploy.yml publishes this documentation on every push to main. Dependabot proposes updates of the GitHub Actions, npm and devcontainer dependencies weekly.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Units. Archives store SI units; forms show lab units. A form field's unit is converted to the schema quantity's unit with pint (archive.py).
  • Python is the reference for rules shared with the page.
  • No build step for the page, and no runtime dependencies in it.
  • Line endings. Keep a file's line endings (most files use LF); a change of line endings makes the whole file show as changed.
  • Tests come with changes: Python tests in tests/, JS tests in tests/js/, the parity fixture regenerated when the rules change.
