docs.title: Contribute to the documentation
docs.text: The documentation is written in Markdown in docs/ and built with MkDocs and the Material theme. It is published to GitHub Pages on every push to main (.github/workflows/mkdocs-deploy.yml).

docs.title: Preview your changes
docs.text:
From the plugin folder (the docs tools are in the dev extras):

uv run --extra dev mkdocs serve -a 127.0.0.1:8001   # live preview; NOMAD uses port 8000
uv run --extra dev mkdocs build --strict   # fails on broken links, as a check

docs.title: Where things go
docs.text:
The pages follow the Diátaxis structure: each kind of page answers one kind of question. Put new content where its reader looks for it.

Page Answers Write Tutorial "How do I start?" One complete first run, step by step, with no choices. How-to guides (docs/how_to/) "How do I do X?" Instructions for one task each: using the logbooks, the dashboards, recipes, installing, contributing. Explanation "Why is it like this?" The reasons behind the data model, the read-only fields, the dashboards. Plugin structure "Where is what in the code?" The map for developers: parts, flows, checks, tests, where to change things. Reference "What exactly is field X?" Every section and field, with its unit and whether it can be edited.

A new page must also be listed under nav in mkdocs.yml, and linked from the home page if readers should find it from there.

docs.title: Keep the docs in step with the code
docs.text:
Update the docs in the same pull request as the change:

You changed Update A section or field of a schema Reference; the how-to guide that uses it A field or behaviour of a dashboard Use the logbook dashboards A module, endpoint, check, test file or CI job Plugin structure How to develop or test Contribute to this plugin A design decision Explanation

docs.title: Style
docs.text:
• Write for the lab's users in the guides and for developers in the contributing guide and the plugin structure; say who a page is for when it is not obvious.
  • Use the names the form shows (Laser details, Process steps) for users, and the code names (LaserCalibration, steps) for developers.
  • Give units as the form shows them, and say when a value is stored in another unit (see Units).

  • Use admonitions for what readers must not miss:

    !!! warning "Title"
    Text, indented by four spaces.

  • Link to other pages with relative paths to their .md file, e.g. [Reference](../reference/references.md); mkdocs build --strict reports links that do not resolve.

docs.title: Contribute to This Plugin
docs.text: New to the code? Start with Plugin structure: the parts of the plugin, how they talk to each other, what is checked where, the tests, and where to make a change. This page has the recipes for common changes.

docs.title: Code layout
docs.text: Module Contents pld_deposition.py PLD logbooks (PLDLogbook, SAPLDLogbook, LAPLDLogbook), process steps, target selection, recipe loader, and the save logic (normalize) sps_deposition.py The SPS logbook (SPSLogbook), its process steps, plasma and target selection, and its save logic process_steps.py Steps shared by all systems: GasProcessStep (pressure, gases, valve), HeatingStep, CoolDownStep base_sections.py What every logbook adds to the native NOMAD process: the operator, and a name when none is given references.py Comparing and copying references between entries laser.py LaserCalibration (with the T1 calculation) and LaserParameters gas.py BackgroundGas, the gases and atmospheres stages.py HeaterStagePosition, TargetStage, CartesianHeaterScan, PolarHeaterScan sample.py System-agnostic samples: the Sample entry, the SubstrateType entry (the substrate database), SampleInRun, Layer, the SampleRun base of a run, sample_id() and sample_name() target.py Target, and the PLDTarget and SputterTarget database entries in_situ.py In-situ techniques: reading and plotting exported RHEED and MIC files, the LA-EDS energy axis composition.py Chemical formulas of targets and substrate types, and the elements NOMAD's search uses database.py The target and substrate database: the one upload that holds every target and substrate type schema_packages/schema_package.py Imports all modules and initialises the schema package dashboards/ The PLD and sputter logbook dashboards, see below

docs.title: Develop and test
docs.text:
Develop in nomad-distro-dev, with the plugin in packages/differ-pld4energy-schemas (Python 3.10 or newer). From the plugin folder:

uv run pytest            # all Python tests (schemas and dashboards)
uv run ruff check src tests
uv run ruff format src tests

The tests work from any folder (also from the distribution root). What each test file covers is listed under Tests and CI; tests/data/example_*.archive.yaml are example entries, which are also tested, and tests/data/exports/ holds small exported data files (RHEED, MIC).

The dashboards' browser code (dashboards/common/static/*.js) is plain JavaScript that the browser loads as ES modules, without a build step. It is type-checked and tested with Node 22 or newer, also from the plugin folder:

npm ci                   # once, and after package-lock.json changes
npm run typecheck        # files that start with `// @ts-check`
npm test                 # tests/js/*.test.js

npm run typecheck uses the TypeScript version pinned in package.json. Only files marked // @ts-check are checked, so a script is opted in once its JSDoc types are right.

The validation rules exist in Python (common/rules.py) and in the page (common/static/rules.js), and a parity test keeps them equal. After a deliberate change of the rules, regenerate the expected results and check the page's rules against them:

UPDATE_JS_PARITY=1 uv run pytest tests/dashboards/test_js_parity.py
npm test     # fails until rules.js agrees

In PowerShell, set the variable first: $env:UPDATE_JS_PARITY=1; uv run pytest tests/dashboards/test_js_parity.py; Remove-Item Env:UPDATE_JS_PARITY.

To check an archive file with the full NOMAD processing, run from the distribution root:

uv run nomad parse packages/differ-pld4energy-schemas/tests/data/example_sa_pld.archive.yaml

docs.title: Adding or changing a section
docs.text:
1. Define the section in the module it belongs to, using ELNAnnotation components for editable fields. Store numbers in SI units, with defaultDisplayUnit for the unit shown in the form.
  2. Fields without an ELN component are read-only in the form. Use that only for values that are set in normalize, and say so in the description.
  3. New modules must be imported in schema_packages/schema_package.py.
  4. A new process step must inherit from the step class of its system (SAPLDStep, LAPLDStep or SPSStep), plus a shared base for its content, or it will not be offered in the logbook. Do not let steps of other systems inherit from these classes. Content shared by all systems goes in process_steps.py. Do not override an inherited quantity (e.g. duration) in a content class: with multiple inheritance the system class's version wins; give the quantity its own name instead.
  5. Add tests and update the reference.

docs.title: The shared schema package
docs.text:
All modules share one m_package (from differ_pld4e_schemas/__init__.py). NOMAD renames a package to the module of the last section defined in it. The GUI stores an entry's type as <package name>.<section name> and finds it again by importing that module. schema_package.py therefore renames the package to itself after importing everything and exposes every section there. Entry types are then stored as differ_pld4e_schemas.schema_packages.schema_package.<Section>.

test_section_qualified_names_resolve checks that this keeps working. If you rename a section, entries that already use the old name no longer load.

docs.title: Save logic
docs.text:
PLDLogbook.normalize runs, in this order:

  1. date default and laser details section;
  2. target details: copy target info, check for duplicates;
  3. samples (SampleRun._normalize_samples): sample IDs and names, UUIDs, create the Sample entries of new and external samples;
  4. recipe: copy steps if apply_recipe is ticked;
  5. step targets: fill in a single target, copy target numbers, warn about unselected targets.

NOMAD normalizes sub-sections before their parents, so step-level logic (scan sub-sections, T1) has already run when the logbook's normalize runs.

docs.title: The logbook dashboards
docs.text:
Code: src/differ_pld4e_schemas/dashboards/. Both dashboards serve the same page and share everything that does not depend on the system; each has its own form definition, rules and converter.

File Contents pld_logbook/, sputter_logbook/ One dashboard each: .../__init__.py Dashboard entry point .../spec.py Form definition, including client: the page's texts and settings (title, draft folder, film steps, ...) .../rules.py The dashboard's LogbookRules (film steps, systems whose steps have a sample mask, extra computed values) .../convert.py The dashboard's LogbookConverter, with the sections only it has (PLD: laser, in-situ; SPS: general comments) .../app.py Creates the app with common.app.create_app common/app.py FastAPI app: serves the page, api/spec, api/validate, api/archive, api/draft-name, api/form-from-archive common/rules.py LogbookRules: computed values, section requirements, validation, draft checks common/convert.py LogbookConverter: form ⇄ archive for run, samples, system details, targets and steps; file and draft names common/static/ The page, no build step: index.html, style.css and ES modules: app.js (the page: form, NOMAD lookups, dialogs, save, drafts), rules.js (computed values and validation, mirroring rules.py), charts.js (plots of exported data files), nomad-api.js (requests to NOMAD and to the dashboard), pdf.js (PDF export), dom.js (el()), config.js (URLs), util.js, constants.js common/fields.py field(), number(), comments() common/steps.py Field groups of every system: gases, pressure, temperature, heating and cool-down common/values.py Conditions (evaluate), reading form values common/archive.py Form values ⇄ archive quantities, unit conversion common/samples.py The Samples section: fields, sample IDs and names, Sample files

The scripts must not name a system: what differs between dashboards comes from the spec (client, section intros, variant keys).

docs.title: Add or change a dashboard field
docs.text:
Most changes only touch spec.py:

number(
    'spot_size',  # key in the form data
    'Spot size',  # label
    'mm^2',  # unit the user types in (pint)
    unit_label='mm²',  # how the unit is shown
    archive='laser.spot_size',  # quantity path in the schema section
    visible_if={'key': '/run/system', 'equals': 'LA-PLD'},  # optional
)
  • The quantity must exist in the schemas; values are converted to its unit. test_spec_archive_paths_exist_in_schema checks every step field, and test_spec_section_archive_paths_exist_in_schema the other sections.
  • Fields are required unless required=False (textarea, bool, computed, rows and files fields are optional by default).
  • Choices that also exist in the schema are checked against it by test_spec_choices_match_schema.

Field kinds: text, textarea, number, integer, select, bool, date, time, reference (an entry from NOMAD: a target, sample or substrate type), target_choice and sample_choice (one of the targets or samples of the form), step_choice (process steps of the form), rows (a repeating sub-section, with columns), files (uploaded files, optionally with a chart) and computed. A reference can copy values of the chosen entry into the form with ref_copy (e.g. the material of a target), and required_if makes a field required only while a condition holds.

Every field key and kind is listed in the docstring of common/fields.py and in KNOWN_KINDS and FIELD_KEYS there; tests/dashboards/test_spec_contract.py fails on a key or kind it does not know, so a misspelt key is caught. Add a new key in both places.

docs.title: Steps and sections
docs.text:
• A PLD step variant is made with variant(label, sections, fields, laser=...):
    • laser='required', 'optional' or 'none' says whether the step needs the laser. For 'optional', pass the keys of its laser fields in laser_keys: they get a Laser used switch.
    • prefill_from='pre_ablation' makes a new step start with the values it shares with the last step of that variant.
  • An SPS step variant says with target='required' that it sputters a target.
  • A section with requirement={'from_steps': 'laser'} (SPS: 'target') is required, optional or not needed depending on the steps (common.rules.section_requirement). A section that is not needed is neither validated nor saved.
  • count_control: True on a list section adds a "how many" input.

If you add a new kind of field, condition, rule or computed value, implement it in both the Python side (common/ or the dashboard's rules.py) and common/static/rules.js, and add tests (tests/dashboards/, tests/js/).

docs.title: Run the dashboard
docs.text:
• Tests: uv run pytest tests/dashboards and npm test
  • In NOMAD: restart uv run poe start and open http://localhost:8000/nomad-oasis/dashboards/differ_pld4e_schemas-pld-logbook/ or .../differ_pld4e_schemas-sputter-logbook/. Restart NOMAD after any change, to static/ too: the page compares the version of its files with the one the server took when it started, and until a restart it asks for one instead of running against an old form definition.
  • The dashboards need the target and substrate database upload (database_upload_id, see Configuration).
  • A dashboard whose URL answers 404 failed to load: see When the dashboard does not load.

When you change a schema quantity the form uses (rename, unit, choices), update spec.py in the same change; the dashboard tests fail until both agree.

docs.title: Git workflow
docs.text:
The plugin has its own repository (timval-differ/differ-pld4energy-schemas), which nomad-distro-dev includes as a git submodule in packages/differ-pld4energy-schemas. Work in the plugin folder as in any repository:

  1. Branch from main (git switch -c fix/…).
  2. Commit, with tests and the documentation in the same change, and push.
  3. Open a pull request in the plugin repository. CI must pass (install-and-test, dashboard-scripts, ruff-linting).
  4. After the merge, update the distribution to the new plugin commit: in the distribution root, git -C packages/differ-pld4energy-schemas switch main, git -C packages/differ-pld4energy-schemas pull, then commit the changed submodule pointer (git add packages/differ-pld4energy-schemas).

Keep each file's line endings (most files use LF): an editor or script that changes them makes the whole file show as changed in the pull request.

docs.title: In a local development setup (nomad-distro-dev)
docs.text:
Development happens in the lab's distribution, timval-differ/nomad-distro-dev, a fork of FAIRmat-NFDI's nomad-distro-dev (its upstream; that one does not contain this plugin). The plugin is checked out in packages/differ-pld4energy-schemas. The distribution's README has the full instructions; in short:

  1. Clone the distribution with its submodules (NOMAD itself in packages/nomad-FAIR, this plugin and nomad-material-processing): git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/timval-differ/nomad-distro-dev.git, or git submodule update --init --recursive in an existing clone.
  2. Start the services NOMAD needs (Docker) and write its configuration: uv run poe setup.

  3. The lab's distribution already lists the plugin and its dependency nomad-material-processing in its root pyproject.toml; in another distribution, add them:

    [project]
dependencies = [
    "differ-pld4e-schemas",
    "nomad-material-processing",
    # ...
]

[tool.uv.sources]
differ-pld4e-schemas = { workspace = true }
nomad-material-processing = { workspace = true }

  4. Install: uv sync. The plugin needs Python 3.11 or newer, nomad-lab 2.0.x (2.0.1 or newer) and nomad-material-processing 1.0.x (1.0.7 or newer). The distribution's own requires-python must not allow an older Python.

  5. Set the target and substrate database upload in the distribution's nomad.yaml (database_upload_id, see Set up the target and substrate database). Without it the dashboards cannot offer targets or substrates.
  6. Start NOMAD: uv run poe start. The new entry types appear under Create from schema in an upload, and the dashboards under Dashboards.
  7. For the dashboards' scripts: install Node 22 or newer and run npm ci in the plugin folder (see Contribute to this plugin).

docs.title: When do changes show up?
docs.text:
You changed Do this Python code of the schemas Stop NOMAD and run uv run poe start again. A dashboard: its Python code or its page (dashboards/common/static/) Restart NOMAD, then reload the page. The page asks for a restart until NOMAD runs the same version as its files. nomad.yaml (e.g. database_upload_id) Restart NOMAD. pyproject.toml (dependencies, entry points) uv sync, then restart. A new package in packages/ Add it to pyproject.toml, uv sync, then restart.

Entries that were processed with an older version of the schema are not updated automatically. Save them again in the form, or reprocess the upload.

Every folder in packages/ must be a Python project

The distribution uses packages/* as a uv workspace. A folder there without a pyproject.toml makes every uv command fail with Workspace member ... is missing a pyproject.toml.

docs.title: In a NOMAD Oasis
docs.text:
Add the plugin (and nomad-material-processing) to the plugin dependencies of your Oasis distribution, e.g. as a Git dependency on a released version (a tag), so that a rebuild installs the version you tested and not whatever main is then:

dependencies = [
    "differ-pld4e-schemas @ git+https://github.com/timval-differ/differ-pld4energy-schemas.git@v0.4.1",
]

The plugin needs nomad-lab 2.0.x and nomad-material-processing 1.0.x (pyproject.toml).

Then rebuild and restart the Oasis. Read the NOMAD plugin documentation for the details.

The plugin registers three entry points:

Entry point What it adds differ_pld4e_schemas.schema_packages:schema_package_entry_point The schemas ("PLD4Energy Schemas") differ_pld4e_schemas.dashboards:pld_logbook_dashboard_entry_point The PLD logbook dashboard, at <NOMAD URL>/dashboards/differ_pld4e_schemas-pld-logbook/ differ_pld4e_schemas.dashboards:sputter_logbook_dashboard_entry_point The sputter logbook dashboard, at <NOMAD URL>/dashboards/differ_pld4e_schemas-sputter-logbook/

docs.title: Reproduce a run with a recipe
docs.text:
A recipe is the list of process steps of an earlier run, with all their parameters: pre-ablation, heating, annealing, deposition and cool-down steps, with gases, pressures, temperatures, laser settings and stage positions. Loading a recipe copies those steps into the logbook you are working on, so you can run the same process again on the samples of this run.

There is no separate "recipe" entry type: any earlier logbook of the same PLD system is a recipe. Name your logbooks clearly so you can find good recipes later.

docs.title: When to use it
docs.text:
• Repeat a deposition on a new sample.
  • Make a series of samples with the same process and change one parameter each time.
  • Run the same process on an existing sample again, e.g. a post-processing step.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Create the new logbook (SA-PLD Logbook or LA-PLD Logbook, the same type as the recipe) and fill in the system details, laser details and targets as usual.
  2. Add the samples under samples and save. This creates the Sample entries the recipe will be applied to. An existing sample is added as Existing sample.
  3. Open load recipe and fill in:
    • recipe: the earlier logbook to copy from;
    • sample (optional): one sample to link the copied deposition steps to. If you leave it empty, the deposition steps are linked to all samples of this logbook;
    • tick apply recipe.
  4. Save.

The steps of the recipe are now added to steps. Apply recipe is unticked again and applied recipe shows the name of the recipe that was used.

  1. Go through the copied steps and change whatever is different in this run (see After applying), then save again.

docs.title: What is copied
docs.text:
Part of the recipe Copied? Notes Process steps yes All steps, in order, with all their sub-sections (gases, laser, target stage, heater stage position, scans): how to run them, not what happened in the recipe run (see the next rows). Samples of the deposition steps no Replaced by the sample chosen in load recipe, or all samples of this logbook. The recipe's own samples are never copied, so the new run cannot accidentally be recorded on the old samples. Target of each step yes Steps keep pointing to the same PLD Target entries as in the recipe. Target details only if empty If this logbook has no targets yet, the recipe's targets (including their target numbers) are copied. If you already selected targets, they are kept as they are. Target number in the steps recalculated Taken from this logbook's target details on save. Step name yes Start and end time, duration, comments no They describe the recipe run, not this one. Read-out values (gas flow read-out, actual heater voltage and current) no Set points are copied; read the values of this run off the system. Laser details (calibration) no Calibrate the laser for every run. System details (date, base pressure, carrier, particle reduction plate) no Samples no In-situ techniques no

The copy is a snapshot. Changing the recipe logbook later does not change the logbooks it was applied to. The recipe field keeps the link to the recipe, so you can always see where the steps came from.

docs.title: After applying
docs.text:
Check after every recipe:

  • Targets. If the recipe uses a target that is not in this logbook's target details, the step gives a warning on save and its target number stays empty. Add the target under targets, or pick another target in the step.
  • Target numbers. Targets move, so check the target numbers in the target details. The steps take their target number from there.
  • Samples. All copied deposition steps are linked to the same samples. In an LA-PLD logbook with several samples, change the sample of the steps that belong to another sample.
  • Start and end times, comments and read-out values are empty: fill them in for this run.

docs.title: Things to know
docs.text:
• Same system only. An SA-PLD recipe can only be applied to an SA-PLD logbook and an LA-PLD recipe only to an LA-PLD logbook: the step types differ. Selecting a recipe of the other system gives an error and nothing is copied. The recipe picker may also list other process entries, such as SPS logbooks. Choose a PLD logbook.
  • Steps are added, not replaced. Steps already in the logbook stay and the recipe steps are added after them. Delete steps you don't need.
  • Applying twice adds the steps twice. Apply recipe is unticked after each copy, so saving again does not copy again. But if you tick it again, the steps are added a second time.
  • No recipe or no samples. Without a recipe, ticking apply recipe gives an error. Without samples (none chosen and none in this logbook), the steps are copied and their samples stay empty. Fill them in afterwards.

docs.title: Example: a series on new samples
docs.text:
Run 1 is the reference run, STO on Si. For run 2:

  1. Create an SA-PLD Logbook STO on Si (repeat), fill in date, base pressure, carrier and laser details.
  2. Add a new sample on Si 1" with flat with a 20 nm SrTiO3 film, and save. This creates SA-PLD_<date>_<time>_S01.
  3. Under load recipe select STO on Si, leave sample empty, tick apply recipe and save.
  4. All steps of run 1 are now in run 2. Their deposition steps are linked to SA-PLD_<date>_<time>_S01, and the targets of run 1 are selected. Change the target numbers if the targets moved, and change the number of pulses if this sample should be thicker.

docs.title: In an archive file
docs.text:
You can also apply a recipe from a YAML or JSON archive file. A logbook in the same upload is referenced by its file name:

data:
  m_def: differ_pld4e_schemas.schema_packages.schema_package.SAPLDLogbook
  name: STO on Si (repeat)
  load_recipe:
    recipe: '../upload/archive/mainfile/sto_on_si.archive.yaml#data'
    apply_recipe: true

docs.title: Use the logbook dashboards
docs.text:
The plugin has two logbook dashboards, guided forms for the logbook of one run:

  • PLD logbook for SA-PLD and LA-PLD runs;
  • Sputter logbook for SPS runs (see The sputter logbook).

They work the same way. Each saves the run as normal entries of this plugin's schemas: an SA-PLD, LA-PLD or SPS logbook, plus a Sample entry for each new or external sample. Everything they save can afterwards be viewed and edited in NOMAD as usual; see Use the PLD logbooks. This page describes the PLD logbook first.

Compared with the NOMAD entry editor, the dashboards:

  • start each run with the samples it makes or processes;
  • show only the fields that apply to your choices (system, process steps, scan type, gases, plasma, in-situ techniques, ...);
  • ask for the targets (and in the PLD logbook the laser details) only when a process step needs them;
  • only save the logbook when every required field is filled in; until then the run can be kept as a draft;
  • convert lab units (mbar, mJ, °C, mm, nm, ...) to the units NOMAD stores.

docs.title: Open it
docs.text:
Log in to NOMAD first. Then open PLD logbook or Sputter logbook from NOMAD's dashboards menu, or go to <NOMAD URL>/dashboards/differ_pld4e_schemas-pld-logbook/ or <NOMAD URL>/dashboards/differ_pld4e_schemas-sputter-logbook/ (locally: http://localhost:8000/nomad-oasis/dashboards/differ_pld4e_schemas-pld-logbook/).

It opens on the start page:

  • New logbook starts an empty form.
  • Continue current logbook returns to the logbook you were working on in this browser, whether saved or not.
  • Drafts lists the drafts in your unpublished uploads; click one to continue it.
  • Recent logbooks lists your latest logbooks; click one to open it. Find a logbook… searches all logbooks you can see.

Opening another logbook or draft asks first if it would replace a logbook you are working on. Start page in the top bar (or a click on PLD logbook) takes you back; the form stays as it is.

docs.title: Fill in a run
docs.text:
Work through the sections on the left; Next takes you to the next one. The number next to a section is the number of things still missing there, and a green tick means the section is complete. Missing fields are marked once you leave a section with Next, or straight away for fields you have edited.

  1. Run. Your name and email are filled in from your NOMAD login; change them if someone else does the run. Choose the PVD system: it decides which carriers, scan options and fields are offered. Enter the date and start time of the run, or press Now when you start it. They are on the lab clock (Europe/Amsterdam), whatever time zone your computer is set to, and make up the sample IDs. The run name is optional.

  2. Samples. List the samples you make or process in this run. Set Number of new and external samples to add or remove samples in one go. For each sample choose:

    • New sample (most runs): pick the substrate from the substrate database.
    • External sample: a sample prepared elsewhere, without a sample ID. Pick its substrate, or leave the substrate empty and describe it under Substrate details. Under Films already on the sample list the films it came with, from the substrate up (material and, if known, thickness). Put anything else you know about it in the comments.
    • Existing sample: a sample made earlier with a PLD4Energy system, e.g. for an extra deposition, annealing or only characterisation. Pick it from the list.

    Substrates are only chosen from the target and substrate database, which only maintainers can change (see Set up the target and substrate database). Is a substrate missing? Ask a maintainer. Maintainers see New substrate in the database below the samples; it asks for the material name and its chemical formula (e.g. SrTiO3), which makes the samples searchable by element, and saves it in the database upload. New and external samples get a sample ID system_yyyy-mm-dd_hh:mm_S## (S01, S02, ... in the order of the list, after the samples already saved: a removed sample's number is not given again) and a sample name made from the substrate and the films grown on it, e.g. SrTiO3_YSZ-20nm_SrRuO3-50nm. The films come from the deposition steps (see below), so the sample name changes once the (desired) film thickness is entered under Process steps. Existing samples keep their own ID. 3. System details. The substrate carrier and the base pressure of the main chamber. LA-PLD also asks for the particle reduction plate. 4. Targets and 5. Laser details. Only needed when a process step uses the laser (pre-ablation and deposition). Without such a step they show as not needed in the list on the left, and nothing entered there is saved. - Targets: pick each target in the system and its target number (its position, 1 to 5) for this run. The dashboard cannot add PLD targets: a maintainer adds a new target as a PLD Target entry in the target and substrate database upload in NOMAD, with its chemical formula, shape and size, density and the ID engraved on its back (see Reference › PLD Target). - Laser details: enter the energies before and after the chamber. The 1st window transmission is calculated as you type; switch on Enter the 1st window transmission manually to type your own value instead. 6. Process steps. Add the steps in order with the + ... buttons: pre- ablation, heating, annealing, pulsed laser deposition and cool-down. Each step can be moved up or down, removed, and folded away with a click on its title. A run without deposition (e.g. only annealing or only characterisation) is fine. - Time: the start and end time of each step, in 24-hour hh:mm (e.g. 14:05; 1405 or 14.05 is turned into that), as in the system log, so the pressure, temperature, ... of the step can be found in the logs later. The date is that of the run; a time after midnight is taken as the next day. Both times are optional. A new step starts at the end time of the step before it; change it if there was a pause. An end time before the start time is an error. A step that starts before the step before it ends gets a warning, but can still be saved. A prefilled step or a recipe does not copy the times. - Background gases: choose UHV to record only the chamber pressure, or Background gas and tick each gas to fill in its set and read-out flow (at least one gas must be ticked). All gases share one valve, so its position (0 closed to 1000 open) is entered once per step. - Target stage: start x, y and z position, offsets, scan width and scan speed in x and y. - Temperature control (heating, annealing, deposition and cool-down): the fields follow the Temperature control panel of the system software. Tick Fix output and Drift compensation as set there. A heating step also has Ramp on: its ramp rate is only asked for when the ramp is on. Annealing and cool-down steps always ask for the ramp rate. Deposition steps have no ramp. - SA-PLD: choose the heating mode. Laser heating (PID) takes the setpoint in °C and the ramp rate in °C/min, and asks for the heater output (%) once the setpoint is reached. Laser heating (power) takes the setpoint in % and the ramp rate in %/min. Also note the laser output limitation set with the knob (50% unless changed). - LA-PLD: setpoint in °C and ramp rate in °C/min, plus the set and actual voltage and current of the main heater power supply. - Pulsed laser deposition: a new deposition step starts with the target, target stage, gases and laser settings of the pre-ablation step before it; change what differs. Enter the film thickness, in nm or, with Thickness given in set to pulses, as a number of laser pulses (the sample name then shows e.g. YSZ-1500p). Each deposition step grows one film, of its target's material, on its samples, and these films make up the sample names. In the SA-PLD a deposition covers the samples ticked under Samples covered (all by default): untick those shielded by a sample mask. In the LA-PLD choose the sample. The target and heater stage fields follow the Manual movement and Define scan pattern dialogs of the system software; choose the heater scan type (Polar scan is the default) to get its scan fields. 7. In-situ techniques. Optional. For each measurement: + Add measurement, choose the sample, tick the process steps it was taken during, then switch on each technique you used and add its data files. A file field takes several files of its format, e.g. a series of RHEED .png images. Files can also be added later: a technique without files is saved as awaiting data. A file never replaces another one: a name used twice gets a number, e.g. step1 (2).txt. 8. System logfiles. Optional: add the .txt logfiles exported from the TSST software. 9. Review and save. Lists everything that is still missing; click an item to jump to the field. Choose an upload (or + New upload) and save.

Saving creates the Sample entries first and then the logbook, and shows NOMAD's processing messages. After saving, the form stays open: saving again updates the same logbook and its samples.

docs.title: Drafts: continue on another computer
docs.text:
A run often spans several computers, and a logbook can only be saved once it is complete. To keep an unfinished run, use Save draft (top bar or Review and save). It needs the system, date and start time, and an upload.

  • The draft is stored in the upload as pld_drafts/<run>.draft.json (sps_drafts/ for the sputter logbook), together with the in-situ files you picked. It is not an entry: it does not show up in searches and does not count as logged. Only the saved logbook does.
  • On another computer, the start page lists the drafts in your unpublished uploads; pick one to carry on.
  • If someone saved the same draft elsewhere after you opened it, you are asked whether to overwrite it or to load their version. Cancel keeps your form and does not save the draft.
  • Saving the complete logbook deletes the draft.

Independently of drafts, the form is kept in your browser while you work, so you can close the page and continue later on the same computer. It is kept per NOMAD user: on a shared computer, the next user does not get your form. Files you chose but did not save yet are not kept: choose them again. New logbook on the start page clears the form.

docs.title: Export as PDF
docs.text:
Export as PDF (top bar, or Review and save) turns the logbook in the form into a report and downloads it as a PDF file, named after the run. The report lists every section and step with the values that apply, in lab units. Sections the steps do not need are left out.

Any logbook can be exported, saved or not. Unless it is a complete logbook that was saved to NOMAD, the report says DRAFT / INCOMPLETE: this is not a logged logbook at the top, with the number of things still missing. The PDF is saved on your computer only; the logbook in NOMAD remains the record.

docs.title: Add in-situ data later
docs.text:
In-situ data often has to be collected from other computers after the run. Save the logbook without the files: the techniques show as awaiting data in the dashboard and in NOMAD. Later, open the logbook from the start page, add the files under In-situ techniques and save again. The same goes for the system logfiles.

Logbooks saved before measurements had a sample and process steps open with their techniques as one measurement: choose its sample and steps before saving again.

docs.title: Repeat a run (recipe)
docs.text: Choose the PVD system, then under Process steps click Load steps from a recipe… and pick an earlier logbook of the same system. Its process steps are added after your current steps; if you have not selected any targets yet, its targets are taken over too. Samples are not copied: the steps apply to the samples of this run (in the LA-PLD, choose the sample of each deposition step). Neither are the step times, comments or read-out values (gas flow read-out, actual heater voltage and current) of the recipe run: fill them in for this run. The sputter logbook does not record which recipe its steps came from; saving says so.

docs.title: Change a saved logbook
docs.text:
Opening a saved logbook from the start page loads it into the form. Saving overwrites it and updates the Sample entries it created; samples from other runs are never changed. A sample keeps its ID once its entry exists, even if you change the date or time of the run. The logbook must be in an upload you can edit (not published).

What the form does not show is kept: values added to the logbook (outside its process steps, which come from the form as a whole) or to its Sample entries in NOMAD's entry editor (for example a lab ID, tags or references) stay when you save again. What the form shows comes from the form, also when it is empty there: the comments of the run and of a sample are the description of the logbook and of the Sample entry. Sample entries are updated without checking for changes made in NOMAD. If the logbook was changed in NOMAD after you opened it, saving asks whether to overwrite it or to save the form as a new logbook. A logbook with process steps the dashboard cannot show is not overwritten: save it as a new logbook, or edit it in NOMAD.

docs.title: The sputter logbook
docs.text:
The Sputter logbook is filled in like the PLD logbook, with these differences:

  1. Run. The PVD system is always SPS. Sample IDs are SPS_yyyy-mm-dd_hh:mm_S##.
  2. Samples. As in the PLD logbook. The sample names come from the sputtering steps, e.g. Si_Ta-50nm_Ti-10nm.
  3. System details. The substrate carrier (4" carrier SPS, 1 cm² sub plate or Fixed stage) and the main chamber pressure. With the fixed stage, say whether a mask is used and which one.
  4. Targets. Only needed when a step sputters (pre-sputtering or sputtering). Pick each target and its position: positions 1 and 2 take 2" targets, position 3 a 4" target. Targets come from the sputter target database, separate from the PLD targets. Maintainers see New target in the database, which asks for the chemical formula and the diameter in inch. NOMAD warns on save when a target does not fit its position.
  5. Process steps. Pre-sputtering, heating, sputtering and cool-down. For a multilayer, add a pre-sputtering and sputtering step per layer.
    • Plasma: choose DC, RF or DC+RF. DC asks for the voltage U, RF for the load capacitance CL, DC+RF for both. The current I and the DC bias are optional; the power is required.
    • Power ramps (ramp up, ramp down) are entered in W per 5 minutes, as in the lab. NOMAD shows them in W/min: 10 W/5 min is 2 W/min.
    • Sputtering: a new sputtering step starts with the target, gases and plasma of the pre-sputtering step before it. Enter the heater position (x, y, z, spin), heater rotation, shutter, sputter time and the film thickness. A sputtering step covers the samples ticked under Samples covered (all by default): untick those shielded by a sample mask. Sputtering currently does not support a heating step.
  6. General comments. Anything else about the run.

There is no laser and no in-situ section.

docs.title: Good to know
docs.text:
• Required fields are marked with *. Comments are optional. A field with only spaces counts as empty.
  • Numbers take a dot or one comma for decimals: 1.5 and 1,5 are the same. A comma that may separate thousands, as in 12,000 or 1,500, is refused: write 12000, or 12 if twelve was meant.
  • The dashboard checks the form again on the server before anything is saved.
  • Targets and substrates come only from the target and substrate database upload; View the database in NOMAD (Edit for maintainers) opens it.
  • New targets and substrates added to the database in NOMAD appear when you start a new logbook or open Samples or Targets; Refresh lists reloads them at any time.
  • Targets and substrates that are switched off as out of stock in NOMAD are not offered. A logbook that already uses one keeps it, marked (out of stock).
  • A new logbook never overwrites an existing file: if a logbook with the same system, date, time and run name, or a sample with the same sample ID, already exists in the upload, saving stops with a message.

docs.title: Use the PLD logbooks
docs.text:
Short guides for the everyday tasks. For a complete walk-through of a run, see the tutorial. For every field and unit, see the reference.

Save to update

Calculated and copied values (sample IDs and names, 1st window transmission, target numbers, copied recipe steps, ...) are updated when the entry is saved, and the checks run at the same time. Messages appear after saving.

docs.title: Set up the target and substrate database
docs.text:
All targets (PLD and sputter) and substrate types are kept in one upload, the target and substrate database. Only maintainers create, edit and delete them; everyone else can only view them and choose them in a logbook. NOMAD grants edit rights per upload, so this is arranged with the upload's members:

  1. A maintainer creates an upload, e.g. PLD4Energy targets and substrates, and adds the targets and substrate types to it (see below).
  2. In the upload's members, add the other maintainers as coauthors (or a maintainers group as coauthor group): they can edit the upload. Add everyone else who writes logbooks as reviewers (or a group of all lab members as reviewer group): they can see the entries but not change them.
  3. Do not publish the upload: a published upload can no longer be edited, also not by maintainers.

  4. Put the upload ID in nomad.yaml and restart NOMAD:

    plugins:
  entry_points:
    options:
      differ_pld4e_schemas.schema_packages:schema_package_entry_point:
        database_upload_id: <upload id>

From then on:

  • the logbook dashboards only offer targets and substrates from this upload, and refuse others on save. New target / substrate in the database is only shown to maintainers and saves the new entry in this upload;
  • a PLD Target, Sputter Target or Substrate type entry created in any other upload gives an error on save, and logbooks and samples that refer to a target or substrate outside the database get a warning;
  • an external sample on a substrate that is not in the database is not a reason to add one: leave its substrate empty and describe it under substrate details.

Without database_upload_id no targets or substrates can be chosen in the dashboards: they tell the user that the database is not set up.

docs.title: Manage the target database
docs.text:
Every physical target is one PLD Target entry, in the target and substrate database upload. Only maintainers add or change them.

  • Add a target: create a PLD Target entry with material, chemical formula, manufacturer and purchase date (optionally the engraved Target ID, shape and size, density, purity and a picture of the engraving).
  • Chemical formula: enter the composition with element symbols, e.g. SrTiO3, Fe2O3 or (Y2O3)0.08(ZrO2)0.92 for 8YSZ, not a lab name such as YSZ or STO. NOMAD's search finds the target, and the samples and runs made with it, by the elements of this formula. A formula with unknown elements gives an error on save; see Explanation › Search.
  • Naming: the entry is named after the name field, or after the material if the name is empty. Do not put the target number in the name: target positions change, and the number is entered per run in the logbook.
  • Two targets of the same material: give them different names, e.g. Fe2O3 (Praxair 2024) and Fe2O3 (Pi-Kem 2025), so you can tell them apart in the drop-down.
  • Out of stock: untick in stock when a target is used up or no longer available. It is then no longer offered for new logbooks, but logbooks that used it keep it and their links keep working. Do not delete it: that would break the logbooks and samples that refer to it. Tick it again if it comes back.

docs.title: Manage the substrate database
docs.text:
Every kind of substrate in use is one Substrate type entry, e.g. SrTiO3 10x10 mm, Si 1" with flat, Si 1" without flat, glass or FTO. Samples refer to it. Like the targets, substrate types are kept in the target and substrate database upload, and only maintainers add or change them.

  • Add a substrate: create a Substrate type entry with the material, chemical formula and size (optionally supplier and description). The material is used in the sample names, so write it as it should appear there, e.g. SrTiO3; the chemical formula (e.g. SrTiO3, Si, SnO2 for FTO) makes the samples searchable by element, as for targets.
  • Naming: the entry is named after the name field, or after the material and size if the name is empty.
  • Out of stock: untick in stock when a kind of substrate is used up or no longer available. It is then no longer offered for new logbooks, but logbooks that used it keep it and their links keep working. Do not delete it: that would break the logbooks and samples that refer to it. Tick it again if it comes back.

docs.title: Start a logbook
docs.text:
Create an SA-PLD Logbook or LA-PLD Logbook. Pick the logbook of the system you ran on: it decides which carriers, step types and scan options are offered, and the PVD system field is set by it.

Fill in the operator name and email, the start of the run (datetime, defaults to the first save) and optionally a name. Then list the samples, and fill in the system details: base pressure of the main chamber (mbar) and substrate carrier. For LA-PLD, also set particle reduction plate.

docs.title: Record the laser calibration
docs.text:
The laser details and the targets are only needed for runs with a step that uses the laser (pre-ablation or deposition). The dashboard does not ask for them, and does not save them, for a run with only annealing or characterisation.

Open laser details and enter the energy before and after the chamber (mJ). Transmission of the 2nd window is pre-filled with 92 %.

On save, the 1st window transmission is calculated as T1 = E_after / (E_before × T2):

You did Result on save Entered both energies T1 is calculated (and recalculated on every save). Typed your own T1, manual not ticked Your value is replaced by the calculated one. Typed your own T1 and ticked manual Your value is kept. Ticked manual but left T1 empty T1 is calculated. Energy before chamber is 0 or an energy is missing T1 is not calculated (a warning is given for 0). A T1 calculated before is kept and marked manual, with a warning; untick manual once both energies are entered to calculate it again. The energies give a T1 above 100 % or of 0 % or less T1 is stored, with a warning: check the energies.

T1 and T2 are percentages: the form takes 0 to 100 %.

docs.title: Select the targets of a run
docs.text:
Add one targets entry per target in the system: pick the PLD Target and enter its target number, its position in the system for this run (1 to 5). A number outside 1 to 5 gives a warning. Material, manufacturer and purchase date are copied in on save so you can check your choice.

Checks: selecting the same target twice is an error; using a target number twice is a warning.

docs.title: List the samples of a run
docs.text:
A substrate is the template a film is grown on; a sample is the substrate with its films. Add one samples entry per sample the run makes or processes:

Origin When Fill in New sample most runs substrate (from the substrate database), films External sample prepared elsewhere, no sample ID yet substrate, or no substrate and substrate details; the films it came with in prior layers; films; what you know in comments Existing sample made earlier in a PLD4Energy system, e.g. for an extra deposition, annealing or characterisation the Sample entry in sample; films grown in this run

The films grown in this run are layers entries, each with the target it is grown from and its thickness (nm); its material is taken from the target. The dashboard fills them in from the deposition steps (one film per step, with the step's target and film thickness); in the entry editor you add them yourself. Films an external sample already had when it came in are prior layers (material and, if known, thickness); they come first in its name and in its Sample entry. The substrate's material and size are copied in as well. On save, for new and external samples:

  • sample ID becomes <system>_<yyyy-mm-dd>_<hh:mm>_S<nn>, from the logbook's start on the lab clock (Europe/Amsterdam); the new and external samples of the run are numbered in order after the highest number already filled in, so a removed sample's number is not given again. A sample ID that is already filled in is kept. Without a start (datetime), the time the entry was created is used, with a warning.
  • name becomes Substrate_Film-<t>nm_Film-<t>nm, e.g. SrTiO3_YSZ-20nm_SrRuO3-50nm, unless you entered one. The name describes the sample; the ID identifies it.
  • sample UUID is derived from the sample ID, so it is the same every time the entry is processed, and kept once filled in. An existing sample takes the UUID of its Sample entry.
  • a Sample entry is created in the same upload (file <sample ID>.archive.json) and linked in sample. The entry records the logbook that made it (made in). If a file of that name was made by another logbook, it is not linked and an error says so: check the start of the run, or enter the sample ID.

For an existing sample, its ID and name are copied from its entry; the entry itself is not changed. Two samples with the same ID give a warning.

The sample entry is created once

After the Sample entry exists, changes to the sample in the logbook are not copied to it by the entry editor. Correct the Sample entry itself. (The dashboard does update the Sample entries it created when you save the logbook again.)

docs.title: Add process steps
docs.text: Add steps under steps in the order they were done. Only the steps of the logbook's own system are offered: pre-ablation, heating, annealing, pulsed laser deposition and cool-down. There is deliberately no sputter step in the PLD logbooks. Add a step type as often as you need; for a multilayer just add another deposition step. A run without deposition is fine.

docs.title: Background gases (every step)
docs.text:
Set atmosphere to UHV when no gas was let in: then only the step's pressure is recorded. Otherwise leave it at Background gas and add one background gases entry per gas that was on:

Field Meaning gas Ar, O2 or N2 set flow flow set on the controller (sccm) read-out flow flow measured / read out (sccm)

All gases share one valve, so the valve is recorded once per step:

Field Meaning valve position valve position on the controller (%) valve position fixed ticked if the valve was kept at a fixed position

Gases listed in a UHV step give a warning.

docs.title: Heating and annealing
docs.text: Heating steps and annealing steps record the heater output (%) once the temperature setpoint is reached. An annealing step also has the dwell time at the setpoint.

docs.title: Target of a pre-ablation or deposition step
docs.text: Pick the target in target. The target number is taken from the target details on save, so the step always shows the current number. If only one target is selected in the logbook, empty step targets are filled in automatically. A step target that is not selected in the target details gives a warning.

docs.title: Laser settings
docs.text: The laser sub-section of pre-ablation and deposition steps holds laser mode, laser voltage (kV), magnification, mask size, spot size (mm²), fluence (J/cm²), energy (mJ), attenuator position (%), frequency (Hz) and number of pulses.

docs.title: Heater stage
docs.text:
Deposition steps have a heater stage position with x, y, z (mm), tilt and spin (degrees), the film thickness (nm) of the film they grow, and list the samples deposited on: in the SA-PLD the samples not shielded by a sample mask, in the LA-PLD the sample of the step.

  • SA-PLD: tick substrate stage scan if the stage scanned. On save a substrate scan sub-section is added for the scan width (mm) and scan speed (mm/s) in x and y. Scan values while the box is unticked give a warning.

  • LA-PLD: choose heater scan type: Polar scan (default) or Cartesian scan. On save the matching sub-section is added:

    Polar scan Unit radius start mm radius stop mm pulse spacing mm max laser frequency Hz number of scans –

    Values in the scan type that is not selected are ignored, with a warning.

docs.title: Target stage
docs.text: Pre-ablation and deposition steps have a target stage sub-section: start x/y/z position, x/y offset, scan width in x and y (mm) and scan speed in x and y (mm/s).

docs.title: Reproduce a run
docs.text: See Reproduce a run with a recipe.

docs.title: Record in-situ measurements
docs.text:
In-situ techniques are a separate part of the logbook (in situ techniques), not part of a step. For measurements that do not belong to a new run, e.g. an older sample that is post-processed, create a stand-alone PLD In-situ Techniques entry. Its sample (a Sample) and process (a logbook) fields are optional.

Data files are often collected from other computers after the run. A technique can be saved without them: its data status is then awaiting data and a warning reminds you, until a file is added (complete).

Add one sub-section per technique (more than one per technique is allowed, e.g. one RHEED entry per capture):

Technique Software Fields RHEED KSA 400 pattern capture: native .img and exported .png; ROI intensity map: native .kdt and exported .txt MIC EZ-Curve native .ezc and exported .csv LA-EDS RSX1000 (later RaySpec RSX2000) .sp0 file, energy offset E0 (eV), energy per channel (eV), number of channels SE, OES, SHG – one data file each

Native files can only be reopened in the instrument software. Upload them anyway: they are the raw data. The exported files can be opened elsewhere.

Exported files are read in any of the encodings instrument software writes (UTF-8, UTF-16 with a byte order mark, or a Windows code page), and with a decimal comma (1,5) in files whose columns are not separated by commas and whose numbers have no decimal point. The columns of a MIC export are converted from the unit in their header (e.g. GPa.nm, 1/km, µm) to the stored unit; a column without a unit is taken to be in the stored unit, with a warning, and a file with a unit that does not fit is not read (a warning says why).

docs.title: LA-EDS spectrum
docs.text:
The .sp0 file has no energy axis; it is rebuilt as E = E0 + channel number × energy per channel (channels counted from 0) and plotted as intensity versus energy.

Not yet automatic

The .sp0 file is not read yet: the location of E0 in the file still has to be confirmed with an example file. Until then the spectrum (intensity per channel) can only be added via an archive file, together with E0 and the energy per channel. With only .sp0 files, LA-EDS stays awaiting data and a warning says the files are not read. The number of channels is taken from the intensity.

docs.title: Write logbooks as archive files
docs.text:
Instead of using the form, you can upload YAML or JSON archive files; see tests/data/example_sa_pld.archive.yaml and tests/data/example_la_pld.archive.yaml.

  • Use m_def: differ_pld4e_schemas.schema_packages.schema_package.SAPLDLogbook (or LAPLDLogbook, PLDTarget, Sample, InSituTechniquesEntry). Steps need their own m_def, e.g. ...schema_package.SAPLDDepositionStep.
  • Numbers are in SI units in archive files, whatever the form shows: Pa (not mbar), J (not mJ), m (not mm), K (not °C), m² for spot size, J/m² for fluence. For example 1e-8 mbar is 1.0e-6, 500 mJ is 0.5 and 700 °C is 973.15.
  • Reference an entry in the same upload by file name: '../upload/archive/mainfile/<file name>#data'.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
All sections of the PLD and SPS schemas with their fields. Unit is the unit shown in the form; archive files take the SI unit (see Explanation › Units). Fields marked generated are filled in on save and cannot be edited (see Explanation › Generated fields).

The m_def to use in archive files is differ_pld4e_schemas.schema_packages.schema_package.<Section>, e.g. differ_pld4e_schemas.schema_packages.schema_package.SAPLDLogbook.

Every entry type extends a native NOMAD section (core basesections or nomad-material-processing, abbreviated nmp), so it has the native fields as well, e.g. name, datetime, lab_id and description, and NOMAD's search finds it (see Explanation › Search).

The dashboard asks for hh:mm and takes the date of the run (the next day after midnight). end_time date/time End of the step, entered like start_time. duration number s Filled in by the dashboard from the start and end time, when both are given. comment rich text Comments. pressure number mbar Chamber pressure during the step. atmosphere choice Background gas (default) or UHV: no gases, only the pressure. background_gases sub-section, repeats BackgroundGas, one per gas. valve_position number Gas valve, shared by all gases: 0 (closed) to 1000 (open). valve_position_fixed yes/no Valve kept at a fixed position.

The steps are native vapour deposition steps (nmp PLDStep, for the SPS PVDStep). On save their native sub-sections are generated from the fields above, read-only:

Shared by all systems (also the SPS).

The PLD heating and cool-down steps add ramp_on (yes/no) and the temperature control fields; the SA-PLD ones also power_ramp_rate (%/min), the ramp rate in power mode. The dashboard only asks for ramp_on in heating steps; a cool-down step always has a ramp rate.

docs.title: PLD Target
docs.text:
Extends the Target section (a native CompositeSystem) and nmp PLDTarget. PLD targets are added by maintainers in the NOMAD entry editor, in the target and substrate database upload (database_upload_id); the PLD logbook dashboard only lets you choose them. A target entry in any other upload gives an error on save.

Field Type Unit Notes name text Entry name. Defaults to the material. Do not include the target number. material text As named in the lab, e.g. 8YSZ; used in sample names. chemical_formula text Required for search, e.g. SrTiO3 or (Y2O3)0.08(ZrO2)0.92 for 8YSZ. Not a lab name: an error on save if it names unknown elements. lab_id text Shown as Target ID: the ID engraved on the back of the target. elemental_composition sub-sections Generated from the chemical formula, with atomic and mass fractions. Hidden in the editor. shape choice Circular (default) or Rectangular. radius number mm Circular targets. Warning on save if missing. length number mm Rectangular targets. Warning on save if missing. width number mm Rectangular targets. Warning on save if missing. diameter number m Generated: twice the radius; empty for a rectangular target. Hidden in the editor. thickness number m density number g/cm³ purity text e.g. 99.999%. manufacturer text purchase_date date/time engraving_picture file Optional picture of the engraved ID. in_stock yes/no Default yes. When no, the dashboard no longer offers it; logbooks that used it keep it.

docs.title: Sputter Target
docs.text: The sputter target database, separate from the PLD targets. Same fields as the Target section (name, material, chemical_formula, manufacturer, purchase_date, diameter, thickness, purity, in_stock); enter the diameter (shown in inch), which decides the positions the target fits.

docs.title: Substrate type
docs.text:
A kind of substrate in the substrate database. Not specific to PLD. Extends nmp CrystallineSubstrate, so the native crystal and electronic properties can be added too.

docs.title: Sample
docs.text:
A sample: a substrate with the films grown on it. Not specific to PLD: system records where it was made. Extends NOMAD's CompositeSystem: its generated components hold the substrate type, and its elements are those of the substrate and the films.

Field Type Unit Notes sample_id text The sample ID; also used as the entry name and, if empty, lab_id. name text Sample name; generated from substrate and layers if empty. datetime date/time Start of the run that made it. description rich text Comments. system text System it was made in, e.g. SA-PLD. origin choice New sample, External sample, Existing sample. substrate reference to Substrate type As in SampleInRun. substrate_details text substrate_material text Generated from the substrate. substrate_size text Generated from the substrate. substrate_batch_number text Optional: batch number of the substrate. layers sub-section, repeats Layer: the whole stack, films it came with first. sample_uuid text Generated once.

docs.text:
One measurement: used as in_situ_measurements in a logbook (one per measurement), and as the stand-alone entry PLD In-situ Techniques (InSituTechniquesEntry).

A native Measurement; its method is In-situ diagnostics, and the techniques used (e.g. RHEED) are added to the entry's searchable methods.

docs.title: Tutorial: your first SA-PLD run
docs.text:
This tutorial walks through recording one complete SA-PLD run in the NOMAD entry editor: SrTiO3 deposited on a Si substrate. You will:

  1. add the target to the target database,
  2. create the logbook and list the samples of the run,
  3. fill in the system details,
  4. add the process steps,
  5. select the targets and fill in the laser details,
  6. attach in-situ data.

The LA-PLD logbook works the same way; the differences are listed at the end. The PLD logbook dashboard guides you through the same steps in a form and only shows the fields that apply.

Saving

Many fields are filled in or checked when you save the entry: the sample IDs and names, the 1st window transmission, the target number in each step, and so on. If a value you expect is missing, save first.

docs.title: 1. Add the target to the target database
docs.text:
Targets are stored once, as their own PLD Target entries, and reused by every run.

  1. In your upload, create a new entry of type PLD Target.
  2. Fill in material (SrTiO3), manufacturer (Pi-Kem) and purchase date. Optionally add diameter, thickness and purity.
  3. Save. The entry is named after the material (SrTiO3). You can set a different name if you have two targets of the same material, e.g. SrTiO3 (Pi-Kem 2024).

Tip

The target number is not part of the target entry. Targets are moved in and out of the system, so the number is entered per run in the logbook. The films of a sample are linked to the target they are grown from, and take their material from it.

If the target already exists, skip this step.

Substrates work the same way: every kind of substrate is one Substrate type entry with its material (Si) and size (1" with flat). Create one if the substrate you use is not there yet.

docs.title: 2. Create the logbook and list the samples
docs.text:
1. Create a new entry of type SA-PLD Logbook.
  2. Fill in the run:
    • operator name and operator email: who does the run;
    • datetime: the start of the run. If you leave it empty it is set to the moment you first save;
    • name: optional, a short name for the run, e.g. STO on Si.

PVD system is already set to SA-PLD and cannot be changed: it is fixed by the logbook type (see Explanation).

docs.title: Samples
docs.text:
A run starts with the samples it makes or processes. A substrate is the template a film is grown on; the sample is the substrate with its films. Add one samples sub-section per sample:

  • origin: New sample (most runs), External sample (prepared elsewhere, without a sample ID) or Existing sample (made earlier in a PLD4Energy system, e.g. for an extra deposition or only annealing);
  • for a new or external sample, the substrate from the substrate database (e.g. Si 1" with flat); an external sample on a substrate that is not in the database gets substrate details instead, and the films an external sample came with go in prior layers;
  • for an existing sample, the sample entry itself;
  • layers: one per film grown in this run, with its target (e.g. SrTiO3) and thickness (nm), e.g. 20 nm. The film material is taken from the target. (The dashboard fills these in from the deposition steps.);
  • comments.

Save. For each new and external sample the plugin then:

  • fills in the sample ID as SA-PLD_<yyyy-mm-dd>_<hh:mm>_S<nn>, e.g. SA-PLD_2026-10-22_09:00_S01, numbering the new and external samples of the run in order after those already numbered;
  • fills in the name from the substrate and films, e.g. Si_SrTiO3-20nm;
  • fills in a sample UUID derived from the sample ID (use it for a QR label);
  • creates a Sample entry in the same upload and links it in sample.

That Sample entry is the sample's identity from now on: deposition steps, recipes and later in-situ measurements refer to it. An existing sample is only linked; its entry is not changed.

Tip

The sample ID uses the logbook's datetime on the lab clock (Europe/Amsterdam), as the dashboard does. Enter the datetime with its offset, e.g. 2026-10-22T09:00:00+02:00.

docs.title: 3. Fill in the system details
docs.text:
• substrate carrier: Omicron carrier or 1" carrier;
  • base pressure of the main chamber (mbar);
  • description for comments.

docs.title: 4. Add the process steps
docs.text:
Add sub-sections to steps in the order you ran them. The logbook only offers SA-PLD steps: Pre-ablation step, Heating step, Annealing step, Pulsed laser deposition step and Cool-down step. You can add each type as often as you need, e.g. deposition, heating, deposition for a multilayer. A run without deposition, e.g. only annealing, is fine.

Every step has:

  • pressure (mbar) during the step;
  • atmosphere: UHV (only the pressure is recorded) or Background gas;
  • background gases: one entry per gas, with the gas (Ar, O2 or N2), the set flow and read-out flow (sccm);
  • valve position (%) and whether it was fixed: one valve for all gases;
  • description for comments.

docs.title: Pre-ablation step
docs.text:
• target: one of the targets of the run (see step 5). If only one target is selected, it is filled in on save. The target number is copied from the target details.
  • substrate temperature (°C);
  • target stage: start x/y/z position, x/y offset, scan width in x and y (mm) and scan speed in x and y (mm/s);
  • laser: laser mode, laser voltage (kV), magnification, mask size, spot size (mm²), fluence (J/cm²), energy (mJ), attenuator position (%), frequency (Hz) and number of pulses.

docs.title: Heating, annealing and cool-down steps
docs.text:
• Heating and cool-down: ramp rate (K/min, which is the same number as °C/min) and temperature setpoint (°C).
  • Heating and annealing: heater output (%) once the setpoint is reached.
  • Annealing: temperature setpoint and dwell time at that temperature.

docs.title: Pulsed laser deposition step
docs.text:
Everything from the pre-ablation step, plus:

  • film thickness (nm) of the film this step grows;
  • samples: the samples deposited on. In the SA-PLD that is every sample loaded in the chamber that no sample mask shields;
  • heater stage position: x, y, z (mm), tilt and spin (degrees);
  • substrate stage scan: tick it if the substrate stage scanned. On save a substrate scan sub-section is added for the scan width (mm) and scan speed (mm/s) in x and y.

docs.title: 5. Select the targets and fill in the laser details
docs.text: These are only needed when a step uses the laser (pre-ablation and deposition). For a run with only annealing, skip this step.

docs.title: Targets
docs.text:
Add one targets sub-section per target loaded in the system:

  • target: pick SrTiO3 from the target database;
  • target number: the position of the target in the system today, 1 to 5.

Save. Material, manufacturer and purchase date are copied from the target entry so you can check you picked the right one. Selecting the same target twice is reported as an error; using the same target number twice gives a warning. Check the messages after saving: a warning tells you, for example, that a step uses a target that is not in the target details.

docs.title: Laser details
docs.text:
Do the laser calibration as described in the section description: attenuator 100% open, 1 Hz, HV NGR mode with HV = 22 kV, 500 mJ, mask 5x18 mm. Then open laser details and enter:

  • energy before chamber and energy after chamber (mJ);
  • transmission window 2: pre-filled with 92 %, change it if needed.

Save. Transmission window 1 is calculated for you as T1 = E_after / (E_before × T2). To enter your own value instead, tick transmission window 1 manual, type the value and save.

docs.title: 6. Attach in-situ data
docs.text: Open in situ techniques in the logbook and add a sub-section for each technique you used: RHEED, MIC, SE, LA-EDS, OES or SHG. Upload the files into the matching fields, e.g. for RHEED the native .img capture and the exported .png. A technique without files is shown as awaiting data, so you can add data collected on other computers later. See Use the PLD logbooks for the details per technique.

docs.title: Differences for an LA-PLD run
docs.text:
Use an LA-PLD Logbook instead. Everything above applies, plus:

  • the substrate carrier also offers 4" wafer carrier and Sample select carrier;
  • particle reduction plate: in use or not in use;
  • a deposition step is linked to the sample it deposits on;
  • the deposition step has a heater scan type, Polar scan (default) or Cartesian scan, instead of the substrate stage scan. On save the matching sub-section is added:
    • polar scan: radius start, radius stop, pulse spacing (mm), max laser frequency (Hz) and number of scans;
    • cartesian scan: x/y offset, scan rate and rotation rate.
